# LoadAtlas

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Textures](Blitz3D-Textures)

</div>


```blitzbasic
LoadAtlas:Int32 file:String, flags:Int32=1, gutter:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | In | String | required | Picture file that contains all tiles. |
| `flags` | In | Int32 | `1` | Texture flags, see LoadTexture. Defaults to 1. |
| `gutter` | In | Int32 | `0` | Pixels of repeated edge color around every tile in the picture. Defaults to 0, which means there are none. |

**Returns:** A texture handle, or 0 if the file could not be loaded.

## Description

Loads a picture as a texture atlas: one image that holds many small pictures (tiles), which [AtlasTexture](AtlasTexture) cuts out as textures of their own. Every tile you cut out shares the one image on the graphics card, so a thousand tiles cost as much memory as the picture itself, and tiles of the same atlas need no texture change between draws.

The flags are the same as for [LoadTexture](LoadTexture). An atlas always clamps at its edges (flags 16 and 32 are added), as a repeating atlas has no use. You can also use the atlas itself as a texture. [FreeTexture](FreeTexture) on the atlas only takes its handle away while tiles made from it exist; the picture is released with the last of them.

**Gutter.** Tiles are drawn from the first mip level only, as the smaller levels mix neighbouring tiles, and are kept half a texel away from their neighbours so that linear filtering does not read them. If you pack the picture with a gutter instead, pass its size in `gutter`: every tile then has that many pixels around it in the picture that repeat the colors of its edge (extruded by your packing tool). The tile rectangles you give [AtlasTexture](AtlasTexture) are the tiles without the gutter. With a gutter, tiles map exactly (no half texel zoom) and, if the atlas has mip maps (flag 8), they use them down to level log2(gutter): a gutter of 1 gives the first level only, 2 gives two levels, 4 gives three, and so on.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
CameraClsColor camera, 70, 100, 160
; A picture of four tiles, 32 pixels each, saved to a file.
sheet = CreateTexture(64, 64, 1 + 4096)
SetBuffer TextureBuffer(sheet)
Color 230, 60, 60 : Rect 0, 0, 32, 32, 1
Color 60, 200, 80 : Rect 32, 0, 32, 32, 1
Color 70, 110, 230 : Rect 0, 32, 32, 32, 1
Color 240, 220, 60 : Rect 32, 32, 32, 32, 1
Color 255, 255, 255
For i = 0 To 3
	Rect (i Mod 2) * 32 + 6, (i / 2) * 32 + 6, 20, 20, 0
	Text (i Mod 2) * 32 + 16, (i / 2) * 32 + 16, Str(i + 1), 1, 1
Next
SaveBuffer TextureBuffer(sheet), "wiki_atlas.bmp"
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
FreeTexture sheet

atlas = LoadAtlas("wiki_atlas.bmp")
For i = 0 To 3
	cube = CreateCube()
	EntityFX cube, 1
	EntityTexture cube, AtlasTexture(atlas, (i Mod 2) * 32, (i / 2) * 32, 32, 32)
	PositionEntity cube, (i Mod 2) * 2.6 - 1.3, 1.3 - (i / 2) * 2.6, 8
	TurnEntity cube, 20, 30, 0
Next
RenderWorld
Flip
WaitKey
```
